deck_title: Biot-Savart B = (mu0*I / 4*pi*rho)*(cos(theta1)-cos(theta2)) finite filament cosine law vs naive infinite-wire 1/rho rig

cards.subtitle: Deterministic Jean-Baptiste Biot & Félix Savart (1820) and Hermann von Helmholtz (1858) finite straight vortex/current filament cosine-difference law (multiplying the infinite-wire 1/rho field by the endpoint subtended cosine factor 0.5 * (cos(theta_1) - cos(theta_2)) = L / sqrt(L^2 + rho^2) = 1 / (1 + u) across hypotenuse aspect excess u = sqrt(1 + (rho/L)^2) - 1 in [0.000, 1.000], locking B_active / B_BiotSavart = 1.0000x across all 17 stations with 0/17 violated) versus naive infinite-wire 1/rho formula (B = B_inf, which overestimates the finite-segment field by sqrt(1 + (rho/L)^2) = 1 + u to 1.2500x at S4, 1.5000x at S8, and 2.0000x at S16 across 16/17 stations) and 64-element dl x r / |r|^3 Biot-Savart line quadrature.

good_fit: 3D polygonal smoke-ring vortex filaments, aircraft horseshoe wingtip vortex lattices (VLM), lightning-arc magnetic pulses, and electromagnetic coil visualizations
Evaluating exact endpoint cosine difference 0.5 * (cos(theta_1) - cos(theta_2)) = L / sqrt(L^2 + rho^2) for every discretized filament segment
Preventing the 2x induced velocity blowup that occurs when applying the infinite-wire 1/rho law to finite segments
not_for: Electrostatic point charges governed by isotropic 1/r^2 Coulomb attraction
